xphoto white balance + intensity_transform tone curves

WHITE BALANCE (cv2.xphoto, wrapped by 'CV White Balance'): the three balancers are genuinely different algorithms, not presets. 'simple' clips the top/bottom clip_percent of each channel's histogram and rescales what is left, so it is driven by the EXTREMES and is fooled by a large saturated region. 'grayworld' assumes the scene averages to gray and only counts pixels below saturation_threshold, so it is driven by the BULK of the image and copes with a blown-out sky. 'learning-based' runs a small regression tree trained on real photos and usually wins on people/skin.
cv2.xphoto.applyChannelGains is the manual escape hatch when you already know the multipliers (gains are per B/G/R, 1.0 = leave alone).

TONE (cv2.intensity_transform): these four are the classic point operations. The cv2 functions write their result into an output argument instead of returning it; the nodes allocate that buffer for you and hand back the finished image.
  gammaCorrection  gamma < 1 lifts shadows, > 1 deepens them.
  logTransform     compresses highlights hard; good for HDR-ish data.
  autoscaling      pure min/max stretch to the full 0-255 range.
  contrastStretching  a piecewise-linear curve through (r1,s1)-(r2,s2).
